question:
DRAG DROP -
Refer to the exhibit. The Cisco Nexus Series Switches SW1, SW2, and SW3 are connected via Layer 2 copper interfaces. An engineer implements loop prevention standard IEEE 802.1w on each VLAN to provide faster recovery from network changes or failures. The implementation has these requirements:
- Interfaces that are connected to Layer 2 hosts must not receive STP BPDUs.
- The implementation must detect unidirectional links due to one-way traffic twisted-pair links.
- Bridge assurance must be enabled between SW2 and SW3.
- The Layer 2 domain must be protected from superior BPDUs that arrive from external switches.
Drag and drop the code snippets from the right onto the blanks in the code on the left to complete the configuration for SW3. Not all code snippets are used.
context: Topology: SW1 (Root Bridge) connects to SW2 (Eth1/4) and SW3 (Eth1/4). SW2-SW3 connected via Eth1/5. SW3 Eth1/6 connects to Layer2 Host. SW3 Eth1/5 also connects to External Switch.
imageNote: Diagram: SW1 (Root Bridge) connects to SW2 and SW3 via Eth1/4; SW3 also connects to a Layer2 Host via Eth1/6 and to an External Switch via Eth1/5.
theory: Cisco's Rapid PVST+ (802.1w) port types let you tune STP behavior per link role: spanning-tree port type network is used on switch-to-switch uplinks and is what actually enables Bridge Assurance, which requires both ends of the link to be in network port type and continuously exchange BPDUs to detect a unidirectional or silently failed link, while spanning-tree port type edge is used on host-facing access ports so they skip STP listening/learning delays and never expect BPDUs from an end device. UDLD aggressive mode is what actually detects a unidirectional link condition on twisted-pair copper by requiring continuous bidirectional echo confirmation, and spanning-tree guard bpdu on the link facing the external switch protects the internal Layer 2 domain by disabling the port if any unexpected or superior BPDU arrives from outside. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — Rapid PVST+ Port Types, Bridge Assurance, UDLD, and BPDU Guard)
